chapter: Lake boats and brass band practice
title: Brass band instrumentation and the arrival of the saxophone
summary: George lists a typical brass band's line-up with no saxophone and says the first sax he played with was Big Ed Washington's.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: What did they have in the band in those days? Say if you had ten pieces or twelve pieces, what was the line of it?

Well they would find two drums, three trumpets, a leaf-like clarinet, and a little mellophone, baritone, the two trombones, and a bass. And the saxes? They didn't have no saxes. They didn't have no saxophone. No sax at all. I never saw no sax.
When did that come in would you say?
Oh, well the first time I played in the band with the saxophone was with, the first man I ever played with in the band was Ed Washington.
Big Ed. Big Ed? Played with, played with Keith Thomas.
Yeah. He was the first man I ever played with with the saxophone in a band. Because I know when I was in the old Eureka band they didn't have any saxophone at all.
